limitations: The graph describes only the candidate revision; deleted predecessor paths are listed, not traversed.

Resolution assumes the repository root is on sys.path and uses case-sensitive tracked .py paths. Installed packages, gitlinks, compiled modules, generated/untracked files, alternate source roots, sys.path/__path__ changes and environment-specific import hooks are not resolved.

All lexical scopes and branches are included, including deferred functions, dead branches and TYPE_CHECKING blocks. Lexical inclusion can overstate runtime reachability; unknown loading can still hide paths.

Recognized dynamic names are direct/aliased importlib.import_module and __import__ calls. Recognized alias meanings are unioned across scopes, with collisions explicitly reported; scope and rebinding are not resolved. Reflection, wrappers, eval/exec and unrecognized loaders can hide imports. Reported dynamic sites cover parsed reached files only.
From-import names may be attributes rather than submodules; both local possibilities are retained. Star exports and nonliteral dynamic names/fromlists remain unresolved.
No first-party module is imported or executed. Imports alone omit configuration, templates, startup effects, service wiring, data/schema dependencies and non-Python consumers.
Unreached does not mean inert. This graph does not prove runtime compatibility, complete release scope, current branch identity, writer custody, deployment permission or production acceptance.
The output guard uses the selected repository's worktree, Git directory and common Git directory. It does not catalogue unrelated repositories or provide an adversarial-filesystem race guarantee.
